Standard: 1.P.AC.3.b
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Competency: Apply knowledge of how the mode and genre of a text affect the types of ideas and information included when reading or creating texts.
Official text: Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact what kinds of ideas and information are included in texts. (I/C)
Skills:
- Apply knowledge of how mode impacts the kinds of ideas and information included in texts.
- Apply knowledge of how genre impacts the kinds of ideas and information included in texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify how different modes (such as print, digital, or multimedia) influence the content of a text.
- Recognize how different genres (such as stories, informational texts, or poems) shape the kinds of ideas and information presented.
- Explain why certain ideas or information are included based on the text's mode and genre.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: mode, genre, text design, audience, purpose, ideas, information
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize how mode and genre influence text content.
- oral_production: Explain orally how mode and genre affect ideas and information in texts.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of mode and genre to understand or create texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain the impact of mode and genre on the ideas and information included in texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by considering how mode and genre affect their content.

Standard: 1.P.EICC.3.d
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Competency: Summarize parts of a text and create visual representations to help understand what is read.
Official text: Summarize and visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding. (I)

- Summarize sections of the text to maintain understanding.
- Visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding.

- Draw or create pictures that represent important ideas from the text.

Required student actions:
- oral_production: Summarize sections of a text orally to show understanding.
- written_production: Create drawings or visual representations of text sections to support comprehension.
- procedural_application: Use summarizing and visualizing strategies during reading to maintain understanding.
- representation_modeling: Model summarizing and visualizing parts of a text to maintain comprehension.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how summarizing and visualizing help maintain understanding of the text.
- comprehension_response: Summarize and visualize sections of the text to demonstrate ongoing comprehension.

Standard: 1.P.AC.3.c
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Competency: Use what you know about different modes and genres to understand how ideas and information are organized in texts.
Official text: Apply knowledge of how mode and genre impact how ideas and information are structured and arranged in texts. (I/C)
Skills:
- Apply knowledge of how mode impacts the structure of ideas and information in texts.
- Apply knowledge of how genre impacts the structure of ideas and information in texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify how the structure of a text changes depending on its mode (e.g., visual, digital, print).
- Recognize how the genre of a text influences the way ideas and information are arranged.
- Explain how the organization of a text helps the audience understand its purpose.
Pedagogy terms / keywords: mode, genre, text structure, organization, audience, purpose
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize how mode and genre affect text structure.
- matching_sorting_sequencing: Sort or sequence examples of texts by mode or genre to show differences in structure.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of mode and genre to interpret text organization.
- representation_modeling: Model how ideas and information are arranged differently in various modes and genres.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how mode and genre impact the structure and arrangement of ideas in texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by describing how their mode and genre shape the organization of ideas and information.
